A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and provide readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D. Content can be matched reliably despite appendix repagination.

before.justification: Sections 5–6 report original formal-language recognition and WikiText-2 language-modeling experiments, with numerical results in Figures 3–4 and Appendix D.

after.justification: Sections 5–6 and Appendix D retain the work's original formal-language recognition and WikiText-2 experimental results.

M1.justification: The transformer architecture, strict causal masks, local attention, and hybrid allocation of global and local heads remain unchanged in Sections 3–6.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same eight synthetic formal languages and WikiText-2 next-token prediction, including the same length-generalization scenarios.

E2.justification: The corresponding experiments retain the same global-only, local-only, and hybrid comparisons. No evaluated comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: Both retain formal-language training lengths up to 40, testing at lengths 41–500 with 512 strings per length, and identical architectures, training budgets, window sizes, positional encodings, and metrics. WikiText-2 settings also remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The analyses of window size, positional encoding, and length generalization are retained with the same evidence. No ablation, robustness test, or case study is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both report five random seeds for formal-language configurations, mean and standard deviation plus maximum results in Tables 1–6, and standard-deviation error bars in Figure 4.

E6.justification: All values in Tables 1–6 match. Figures 3–4 retain identical heatmaps and perplexity curves, and the reported experimental findings and rankings are unchanged.

T1.justification: Theorem 2.7 and its Appendix C.2 proof replace the locally R-trivial syntactic monoid with the syntactic semigroup. Appendix B.2 correspondingly changes the local condition from eMe to eSe. This is a substantive but localized correction: including the monoid identity makes the former condition more restrictive. The other theoretical results and derivations are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about complementary global and local attention, greater hybrid expressivity, the advantage of one-token windows, and empirical support.

C2.justification: The depth-overhead and positional-encoding caveats, interpretations of WikiText-2 results, and limitations concerning small-scale natural-language experiments remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Implementation descriptions, hyperparameters, hardware, runtime, and data information remain unchanged. Appendix D.1 repairs the citation for the already identified Hugging Face codebase without adding implementation settings or access instructions.

R1.justification: v3 adds Wolf et al. (2020), Transformers: State-of-the-Art Natural Language Processing, replacing the unresolved Hugging Face citation in Appendix D.1. The broader research positioning and other cited works remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Appendix B.2 is retitled and locally rewritten, separating R-trivial monoids from locally R-trivial semigroups. Other edits include an introduction paragraph break and expanded bibliographic author names; the overall narrative structure is retained.

P2.justification: Appendix B.2 converts several inline expressions into displayed equations. Subsequent material reflows, with Tables 1–6 distributed across three pages instead of two and Tables 1–2 preceding D.2–D.3. Figure designs and table structures remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 fixes a genuine monoid–semigroup error in the supporting algebraic characterization through consistent changes to Theorem 2.7, Appendix B.2, and Appendix C.2. Clearer definitions and the repaired Hugging Face citation improve correctness and attribution. These are focused improvements; the main transformer–logic correspondences and empirical evidence remain unchanged.
